messages:
evelyn: heads-up: hitting a weird redaction/context leak in the ruby quickstart when running under puma in clustered (pre-fork) mode. DEBUG logs from Puma workers show request_id raw, INFO lines are redacted.

hiro: can you paste a tiny repro + logs?

evelyn: repro: clone github.com/redwood/sample-apps/ruby-telemetry, bundle install, RAILS_ENV=development Puma -w 2 -e development, POST /sessions. Logs: 
```
Puma 5.6.4 starting in cluster mode...
[DEBUG] puma - worker 1 booting - request_id=tmp-555
[DEBUG] rack.request - parsed headers - request_id=tmp-555
[INFO] sessions#create - request_id=REDACTED user_id=42
```
When I run Puma in single-mode (no workers) or use WEBrick everything is redacted correctly.

lucas: interesting. Sounds like the forked worker inherits some thread-local or contextvar-like state and a subsequent OTEL hook that attaches request_id runs later in the request lifecycle. That would let pre-fork logs surface the raw value before redaction filter is attached.

maya: Ruby's typical pattern is to set up logging and filters in an initializer that runs per-process, but if the parent process binds a context value before forking it can leak into children unless reinitialized. Are we doing any global binding at require-time in the quickstart?

evelyn: yes the quickstart's telemetry initializer calls Telemetry.attach_request_hook in an initializer, but we also have a tiny middleware that caches incoming headers in a Thread.current[:req] during parsing so some libs read it early. In cluster mode the fork sequence plus puma worker boot logs cause debug lines to print before our redaction filter wraps the logger in the forked worker.

hiro: two fixes: (1) ensure telemetry init is run in worker boot (on_worker_boot) for puma and reattach redaction filters there, (2) make redaction filter defensive: if a suspicious-looking token/reqid is present in a log message, redact heuristically using regex regardless of attached context. The latter avoids holes for other forked servers.

lucas: +1 on both. For puma we can add a snippet in quickstart's puma.rb: 
```ruby
on_worker_boot do
  Redwood::Telemetry.init if ENV['REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_AUTO_INIT'] != 'false'
end
```

maya: also suggest we add a helper in the ruby SDK expose ensure_fork_safe_init(workers_hook: :on_worker_boot) so quickstarts can use it without copying code. And add a defensive redaction filter that runs a shallow regex redact on anything that looks like a request id or token if our usual context isn't yet present. Make it opt-in via config until we validate false positives.

evelyn: I prototyped the on_worker_boot change and it fixed local reproduction. Also added a small fallback regex that redacts long hex UUID-like tokens in any log message. No false positives in our quickstart logs so far.

lucas: can you file an issue and a PR for the quickstart? Add a CI smoke test that starts Puma in clustered mode in a subprocess, sends requests, and asserts no unredacted tokens appear even with LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG. Reboot worker a couple times to simulate churn.

evelyn: filing now. Will include test and link to PR.

telemetry-bot: Created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/issues/2124 - "Ruby quickstart: Puma pre-fork can cause request_id to leak in DEBUG logs; add on_worker_boot init and defensive redaction" Labels: devex, telemetry, bug.

qa-bot: Smoke test queued for PR #529 - running clustered puma tests.

hiro: follow-up: check Passenger/Phusion and other pre-fork servers for similar behavior. Also add a short section in onboarding: "If using pre-fork servers re-init telemetry in worker boot hooks and prefer defensive redaction until worker init completes."

maya: I'll draft the SDK helper and a doc blurb. Good catch Evelyn :thumbsup:

evelyn: thanks all, will link PR and test results in the issue when CI finishes.
